title: How an order moves through the orders Handler

scenes.title: How an order moves through the orders Handler
scenes.name: The assembly line
scenes.desc: The whole plant, and one order from Submit to the batch

bubbles.html: An Order enters Submit(), passes the three steps of process() and waits in h.batch; the tank tracks pending bytes.

scenes.title: 1 · Submit routes each order
scenes.name: Routing in Submit
scenes.desc: A malformed order is refused; a priority order is written at once

bubbles.html: No ID, customer or lines: Submit() returns ErrInvalid and nothing is stored. intake logs it and reads on.
A KindPriority order skips the batch: Store.WriteBatch writes it at once as WrittenNow.

scenes.title: 2 · The pending-bytes budget
scenes.name: Soft and hard limit
scenes.desc: The soft limit starts shedding; the hard limit stops intake

bubbles.html: At 4 MiB reserve() switches to ModeShedding, and it never goes back. Orders under lowValueCents are now only counted.
At 8 MiB reserve() sets ModeStopped and returns ErrOverloaded. intake stops reading and returns.

scenes.title: 3 · Rewind, then the flush
scenes.name: Otherwise: flush
scenes.desc: Back before the hard limit: the tick writes the batch, and Close repeats it

bubbles.html: The tick writes the whole batch in one WriteBatch call. Bytes leave pendingBytes only on success; a failure keeps the batch.
Pending bytes fall, but ModeShedding stays on. Close() flushes once more when intake ends, even after ErrOverloaded.
